conviction_watchlist.investment_thesis: 作者自述持有100万股以上仓位，多日反复跟踪其100M+ CW DFB激光产能与6家可插拔客户验证，认为其在CW激光短缺中卡位Tier 1激光供应商并向CPO/ELS下游延伸。尽管批评管理层沟通与瑞典市场定位，仍视其为2027-2028光互连转移的高Beta核心暴露。
长期看多存储，强调2026-2027年高端存储需求结构性且经营杠杆显著，HBM/DRAM挤占产能造成全线短缺，2028-2029订单已被预订。作为其H2 2026/2027组合的核心持仓之一。
多日辩护其基本面：80%毛利率预计延续至2030年，NAND存在结构性巨大需求，Phison等指出2027年产能约束比2026年更严重。视其为存储周期中最具弹性的受益标的之一。
被明确列为H2 2026/2027组合核心焦点，与Palantir建立主权AI基础设施合作，算力供需失衡下需求远超供给。属于算力租赁/Neocloud环节的核心多头。
多日反复视为光子学核心持仓，强调其CW激光索取显著价格溢价、Cloud Light并购扩大多倍DC内可服务市场，且可从激光元件向光模块纵向扩张。是'激光器公司不只做激光器'逻辑的代表。
被列为组合核心焦点之一，是AI架构的骨干：所有先进IC/ASIC、COUPE硅光与先进封装均由台积电承担，光引擎与CPO瓶颈之外的唯一不可替代节点。
InP衬底严重短缺、史上最大涨价，作者早年提出并被验证，列为YTD涨幅超100%的核心论点之一（'紫苏叶理论'代表标的）。处于上游材料卡脖子环节并具备定价权。
新建仓位，主打DDR2/DDR3/SLC NAND/NOR等利基存储短缺，7月单月净利年化仅1.9倍P/E，产能向高端迁移导致级联缺货、客户对涨价不敏感。作者认为市场低估其涨价持续性与经营杠杆。
自述持有较大仓位，看好其美国本土800G/1.6T产能溢价与激光/收发器需求严重失衡，但持续对频繁ATM稀释表达不满，属于看好运营但警惕股本结构的中高信心持仓。
H2新论点，切入人形机器人/物理AI下游，以Digit 5新品与Agility(NVDA/AMZN投资)上市为催化。属于早期主题试仓，尚待商业化验证。
InP外延片与量子点代工被Bloomberg点名为半导体关键风险点，公司已与Quintessent签采购协议并推进量子点激光客户送样。属于上游材料卡脖子主题的卫星持仓。
Soitec在光子SOI衬底约95%份额，200M美元收入被描述为'地板'，已有10+客户签产能预留协议，受益2027年硅光放量。典型垄断型卡脖子环节，但尚属布局阶段。
Google TPU 122亿美元协议带来ASIC与光互连双重弹性，Celestial资产切入超大规模CPO项目，且其SVP点出欧洲作为激光来源地间接印证产业链布局。属于中期ASIC赢家组合。
虽然FY27/28营收指引翻倍且CEO确认激光'需求远超供给'，但作者更多将其视为行业供给验证信号，并担忧NVDA投资联发科侵蚀其份额，未表达自身持有或建仓意图。
作为原主要商用激光供应商已停止外销InP激光并转向内部自用，反而成为紧缺市场中的买方，作者仅将其作为供给格局证据而非推荐标的。
引用其CEO关于算力需求远超可建产能的观点支撑AI资本开支论点，但自身仅持有1股且明确对高负债Neocloud的FCF表示保留，属于事件驱动式提及。
提到10月PC CPU涨价10%及可能承接HBM4E基die代工，但SK海力士回应与事实不符，信息存在不确定性，缺乏持续建仓表态。

tweets.original:
Some color on current memory environments for the $MU / $SKHY bros:

"There is zero risk of memory prices dropping" per Team Group GM Gerry Chen. 

- Memory module makers have received notices warning of drastic cuts to their 2027 supply allocations. Some could receive 50% or less of their 2026 allocation.

- Upstream manufacturers have reportedly sold out nearly all of their 2027–2028 capacity.

- DDR5 supply, in particular, is projected to come in at less than 80% of previous expectations.

- Chen expects prices to continue rising 20–30% quarter-over-quarter into 2027 (source Digitimes)

- Chen's commentary on $MU is that even before their new MegaFab capacity comes online Q4 2027 at the earliest, orders for 2028 through 2029 are already fully booked. 

So that there's virtually no relief in sight to current shortages.  

Sharply lower allocations, fully booked capacity into 2029, and future price hikes doesn't quite sound like the AI buildout is slowing down.
tweets.translation:
关于当前内存环境的一些细节，供 $MU / $SKHY 兄弟们参考：

Team Group 总经理 Gerry Chen 表示：“内存价格下跌的风险为零。”

- 内存模组制造商已收到通知，警告其 2027 年供应配额将被大幅削减。部分厂商可能只能拿到 2026 年配额的 50% 或更少。

- 据报道，上游制造商 2027–2028 年的产能几乎已全部售罄。

- 尤其是 DDR5 供应，预计将低于此前预期的 80%。

- Chen 预计，价格将持续环比上涨 20–30%，直至 2027 年（来源：Digitimes）。

- Chen 对 $MU 的评论是：即便其新的 MegaFab 产能最早要到 2027 年第四季度才上线，2028 年至 2029 年的订单也已全部预订完毕。

因此，当前短缺几乎看不到缓解迹象。

配额大幅下降、产能预订已排至 2029 年，以及未来继续涨价，听起来并不像是 AI 建设正在放缓。

I've seen comments from Jim Cramer today supporting hedge funds that short Leopold's "nonsense" $SNDK / $DRAM / SK Hynix type calls.  

As well Cramer calling $CRWD a "Must Buy".   

I'm not sure if Jim Cramer sees a $241B company  labelled "Cybersecurity" and thinks of it as safe... while ignoring all their fundamentals. 

But with Crowdstrike, you have a ~145x FY2028 fwd P/E company, growing revenue 26% Y/Y. That Cramer thinks is a "must buy". 

And then you turn your eyes to the AI capex beneficiary theme that Leopold is long on. 

With names like $SKHY / Samsung in $DRAM... Both FY2027 ~2.8-3x fwd P/E off analyst projections.  

-> Samsung LTAs to 2031 (70% capacity) for durability...  -> Minimum price floor + no price ceiling type contracts from SK Hynix.  
-> Memory shortage much tigher for the next year.  
-> DRAM/NAND % of hyperscaler capex goes higher (est. 68% per Trendforce)  
-> 2027 hyperscaler capex projections all hiked.  

Then with $SNDK, 50% FCF margins, 80% gross margin projections into 2030.   

Only Situational Awareness position I'm in disagreement with is $CRWV due to debt interest eating FCF, but I can make a similar bullish argument with $BE, $INTC, $AMD, and others. 

Not quite sure about short-term, but over the medium run: 

It's hard to not see Leopold's positions pulling an Inverse Cramer due to overwhelming fundamentals.

-> Samsung 长期协议延伸至 2031 年（占产能 70%），提供了持久性…… -> SK Hynix 提供最低价格下限、无价格上限类型的合同。

Especially when both sides have called frontier AI capabilities "cyber nuclear weapons"

It will be theater if any of these parties agrees so publicly, because behind the scenes:

-> They'll likely keep on progressing, whether it's OpenAI, the US Government, or China.

tweets.original:
Anthropic's Economic Scenario publication was a pretty interesting read:

1. Anthropic's "extreme" scenario has GDP growth reaching 15.4% in 2030

So around 7.3x current rates (~2.1% Y/Y), which is consistent with what Elon Musk is saying about outgrowing the national debt with AI.  

2. Almost all of the divergence happens after 2027. 

Their model shows relatively little separation in 2026-2027, then the curves bend sharply into 2028-2030. 

So my read is that it points to 2026-2027 as buildout years and 2028-2030 as economic acceleration. 

Kinda gets mapped as well when you look at $AMZN / $META / $GOOGL capex, and short term FCF headwinds (but massive projected profitability post 2028)

3. In an extreme scenario, unemployment of knowledge workers goes to 17.9%. With 11.9% economy-wide unemployment

"At the individual level, it means coders and call service center agents may have to switch to jobs like electrician and nurse, which are less exposed to AI."

GG computer science majors. 

4. Non-cognitive wages: +33.6% vs. baseline in an extreme scenario. 

So your electricians/construction-type labor becomes extremely valuable? (but this isn't factoring in humanoids yet...)

Whereas -11.5% for knowledge workers in 2030 vs. baseline. 

5. Aggregate capital income is ~81% higher than it would have been without AI

Productivity explodes -> aggregate labor income barely changes -> essentially all of the incremental GDP accrues to capital.

So that makes ownership of capital rather than labor... so equities like compute, power, semis, networking, robotics, etc. become pretty important... 

TLDR:

- Economic growth go brr
- Jobs that require thinking = unemployment + lower wages
- Physical labor = more important, like electricians. 
- AI equities go brrr.
tweets.translation:
Anthropic 的经济情景报告读起来很有意思：

1. Anthropic 的“极端”情景中，2030 年 GDP 增速达到 15.4%。

这大约是当前增速（约 2.1% 同比）的 7.3 倍，与 Elon Musk 所说的 AI 让经济增速超过国家债务增长相一致。

2. 几乎所有分化都发生在 2027 年之后。

他们的模型显示，2026-2027 年差异相对较小，随后曲线在 2028-2030 年急剧弯曲。

所以我的解读是，它指向 2026-2027 年是建设期，2028-2030 年是经济加速期。

当你看看 $AMZN / $META / $GOOGL 的资本开支，以及短期 FCF 逆风（但 2028 年后预计盈利能力巨大）时，也能大致对应上。

3. 在极端情景下，知识工作者失业率达到 17.9%，全经济失业率为 11.9%。

“在个人层面，这意味着程序员和呼叫服务中心客服可能不得不转向电工、护士等受 AI 影响较小的职业。”

GG 计算机科学专业学生。

4. 非认知型工资：在极端情景下较基准增长 33.6%。

所以电工/建筑类劳动力变得极其有价值？（但这还没有把 人形机器人 因素考虑进去……）

而 2030 年知识工作者相较基准为 -11.5%。

5. 总资本收入比没有 AI 的情况下高约 81%。

生产率爆发 -> 总劳动收入几乎不变 -> 本质上所有增量 GDP 都归于资本。

这让资本所有权而非劳动力变得……因此算力、电力、半导体、网络、机器人等股票变得相当重要……

TLDR：

- 经济增长一路狂飙
- 需要思考的工作 = 失业 + 更低工资
- 体力劳动 = 更重要，比如电工。
- AI 股票一路狂飙。

China has many chokepoints such as gallium, graphite, refined lithium, and others + benefits from cost mass production over many future supply chains (eg. robotics). 

If I had to give my opinion on US / China supply chain wars:

- US is trying to achieve Western independence from China/Russia rare earths + materials supply, but took too long (should have been a priority last decade). 

- China is trying to eliminate strategic chokepoint dependence and forcing US reliance on Chinese supply chains (as seen with Wf6) 

It's a race on who achieves supply chain independence first to gain leverage over the other.  

And fun thing is, AI acceleration kinda throws an unknown variable in terms of speeding up independence. 

As well as open source efforts (eg. RISC-V), which China is heavily focusing on. So it's a weird paradox where US should theoretically support open source hardware development + open source AI, but it's also being exploited against them.

From a Chinese perspective, they're pressuring US supply chains by targeting Japan, which increases Western supply chain reliance on China. 

And going down the list to eliminate competitor chokepoints internally by throwing subsidized spend into R&D. Or by acqusition as seen with China's acquisition of EU leaders like Ficontec.  

America... they had all the cards initially, but I think they got too comfortable, and took too long to focus heavily on rare earths (recent funding is a good thing).

The earlier tariffs went the wrong way (socks, furniture, other exports), and pissed off allies in EU/Canada too. 

Which could have been used for leverage for major chokepoints. But maybe they'll realize soon enough why allies are important.

Anyway, we'll see what happens, just my two cents about ongoing dynamics.

In an ideal world, everyone works together... 

TLDR: Just some shower thoughts on how there's an unspoken race on who achieves supply chain independence first to gain leverage over the other.
